text:
CanucksArmy's Wyatt Arndt called it the Jilted Lovers Bowl, and it's hard to improve on that. Vancouver is a year removed from trading Quinn Hughes. Detroit just finished the Dylan Larkin saga, sending its former captain to Montreal after his trade request, with Kirby Dach, Michael Hage and draft picks coming back. Two franchises recently left by their best players met on Wednesday, and the Red Wings looked like the team with less weighing on them, winning 5-1.

Emmitt Finnie made sure of that before most people had found their seats. The 201st pick of the 2023 draft tipped in a Viktor Arvidsson feed at 1:16 and then snapped in a 45% chance from Marco Kasper at 4:05. Lucas Raymond added a power-play goal with 57 seconds left in the first, and Detroit's win chance had already climbed from 53% to 92%. J.T. Compher made it 4-0 in the second off Michael Brandsegg-Nygard. Paul Cotter broke the shutout bid midway through the third, ending a 21-game goal drought per Daniel Wagner of Pass it to Bulis, and Arvidsson tipped home the fifth 42 seconds later. Finnie finished with three points, Arvidsson with three in under 12 minutes, and Moritz Seider had two assists in 24:54.

The score flatters Detroit, though. Vancouver had more expected goals (our measure of chance quality), 3.42 to 3.07, and by our replays of every shot the Canucks deserved to win 56% of the time. The gap was Daniil Tarasov. He stopped 25 of 26 and saved 2.42 goals more than the chances deserved, including a stop on Linus Karlsson 94 seconds in and a 55% look for Cotter in the third. Headlines this week have the Red Wings feeling confident with Tarasov in net, and nights like this explain why.

Vancouver's problems run deeper than one game. Elias Pettersson is seeing a specialist about an injury, Brock Boeser's career year has put him in trade chatter, and Leevi Merilainen allowed five on 26 shots. Detroit has now beaten the Canucks twice, both times by five.
headline: Finnie strikes twice early as Red Wings roll Canucks
